interactivity.rationale: Figure 2 correctly implements the underlying mathematics of camera projection: it dynamically recomputes the image point p as the intersection of the rotated image plane with the fixed 3D ray to world point P, and handles cases where P falls behind the camera. Figure 1 physically fakes this by leaving p rigidly anchored to local coordinates on the image plane, resulting in a physically impossible bent 'projection ray' (Origin -> p -> P) that breaks at p as the plane rotates.

concept.rationale: Figure 2 correctly computes the image point p as the mathematical projection of the 3D point P onto the rotating image plane, keeping the projection ray strictly linear from the origin through p to P.
